meta.title: Toys R Us Wasn't Killed By Amazon. It Was Killed By Its Own Buyout.
meta.hook: Toys R Us paid over $400 million a year in interest before it sold a single toy.
meta.description: In 2005, KKR, Bain Capital and Vornado bought Toys R Us in a $6.6 billion leveraged buyout, financed with more than $5 billion in debt placed directly onto the retailer's own books. Toys R Us was spending roughly $400 million a year just servicing that debt by the time it filed for bankruptcy in September 2017, a collapse that cost about 33,000 jobs. Educational content only, not financial advice.

scenes.narration: Toys R Us paid over four hundred million dollars a year in interest, before it sold a single toy.

visual.query: empty toy store aisle shelves closing
visual.visual_intent: An empty toy-store aisle with sparse shelves, cold fluorescent light, quiet and hollow
visual.decision_reason: hook beat: the ~$400M/yr interest servicing figure, hard cut

scenes.narration: The story people tell is that Amazon killed Toys R Us. That's not really what happened.

visual.visual_intent: Stacked cardboard shipping boxes in a warehouse, representing e-commerce, slightly out of focus

scenes.narration: In two thousand five, KKR, Bain Capital, and Vornado bought Toys R Us for six point six billion dollars.

visual.visual_intent: A boardroom handshake over a deal document, formal and transactional, cold lighting
visual.decision_reason: the $6.6B 2005 LBO transaction value, confirmed via SEC filing and Forbes retrospective

scenes.narration: More than five billion of that purchase was paid for with debt. And that debt didn't sit with the buyers. It landed directly on Toys R Us's own books.

visual.visual_intent: A tall, heavy stack of financial documents on a desk, visually representing debt weight
visual.decision_reason: $5.3B+ debt placed on Toys R Us, standard LBO structure, confirmed via SEC filing / Forbes

scenes.narration: While the company drowned in interest payments, the firms that bought it collected over four hundred million dollars in fees.

visual.query: briefcase money cash close up dark
visual.visual_intent: A briefcase with cash inside, dark and deliberate lighting, contrast to the empty store shot
visual.decision_reason: the ~$464M in fees collected by KKR/Bain/Vornado, confirmed via Forbes reporting

scenes.narration: Toys R Us filed for bankruptcy in September twenty seventeen. About thirty-three thousand people lost their jobs.

visual.visual_intent: A 'store closing' sale sign taped inside a storefront window, blunt and final
visual.decision_reason: Sept 2017 bankruptcy filing, ~33,000 jobs lost, confirmed via Forbes reporting

scenes.narration: The toy store didn't fail at retail. It failed carrying debt it never chose to take on.

visual.query: faded toy store sign exterior building
visual.visual_intent: A faded, weathered store sign on an empty building exterior, closing image of decline
